summary: Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, and studied under Shree Narayan Mishra. He is an Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003-2014), and as senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew Ollett specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (~2008-2009) and Columbia University (~2009-2017), and became an Associate Professor at the University of Chicago around 2020.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton III.

Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He has served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard College (~1958-1962) and Yale University (~1962-1967) under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held an academic post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1967 to 2001.
Andrew Watsky is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Oberlin College (~1975-1979) and Princeton University (~1986-1994). He held a post at Vassar College from ~1994 to 2008.
Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist who completed his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg, studying under Harunaga Isaacson, among others. He was appointed Professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

Andrey Terentyev specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970-1975) and held a post at the Museum of History of Religion from ~1978 to 1994.

Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902-1906) and Leipzig University (~1903-1906). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916-1917) and the University of Lviv (1917), which he also founded.

András Róna-Tas specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and served as professor at the University of Szeged (1968-2002) and president of the IATS (~1985-1995).

André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, later holding professorships at EPHE (1956-1973) and the Collège de France (1971-1991).

André Caquot was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and EPHE, later holding posts at EPHE (~1954-1972), the University of Strasbourg (1957-1960), the University of Paris (1964-1968), and the Collège de France (1972-1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Laval University (~1965-1970), EPHE (~1972-1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972-1977), later holding a post at Laval University from ~1979 to 2010.
André Godard was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Beaux-Arts de Paris (~1900-1909) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934-1949).

André Leroi-Gourhan was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Paris (~1929-1944) under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the Musée Guimet (1940-1943), the University of Paris (~1956-1969), and the Collège de France (1969-1982).

André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne (~1928-1937) under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938-1946), Columbia University (~1947-1955), and the University of Paris (~1955-1977).
André Mazon was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900-1904) and Charles University (~1903-1904). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the Institut de civilisation indienne and under teachers including Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe. He directed the Institut français de Francfort (~1953-1959) and held research posts at the CNRS/NCSR.
